ai.description: This frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with dark mottling and possesses prominent, thorn-like tubercles across its dorsal surface, limbs, and eyelids. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes echinatus* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of prominent, conical, spine-like tubercles scattered across its dorsal surface, unlike its smoother relatives.
ai.habitat: The Spiny Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spiny Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal and uses its cryptic, thorn-like skin projections to camouflage against mossy surfaces, effectively hiding from potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes echinatus* exhibits direct development within terrestrial nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of large, yolk-rich eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes echinatus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-elevation forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Spiny Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps from within dense, high-altitude shrubbery in the Western Ghats.
